confidence: uncalibrated neural softmax; threshold picked on validation only
runtime_inputs: declared task family and target yaw
declared target region size and position tolerance
optional declared goal polygon/reference RGB for target location
learned_component: 111107-parameter MLP trained on RGB-derived blue/orange 24x24 masks plus4inspectable statistics. Full-object blue canvas retains occlusion evidence; no exact image-template matching.
geometric_component: Detect green staging polygon and orange silhouette; use declared plane-height correction and region scale; compare center to configured tolerance and silhouette to region. 1.25px center uncertainty and1px footprint margin abstain.
completion_scope: Visual evidence only. Measured release, fresh-frame image-position stability, and controller limits remain separate mandatory gates.
split_unit: Original rendered scene/config seed. Derived occlusions remain in the source split.
offline_label_source: Commanded simulation geometry and known synthetic occlusion. Truth used only offline for labels and external evaluation; never inference.
training_labels_correction: Initial global-blue occluder could target robot pixels. All original occluded-category examples discarded; corrected object-local glyph occlusions regenerated. Original manifest retained. Earlier test reports exploratory; final confirmatory images generated only after model freeze.
limitations: Supports native overhead simulation DUPLO v2 feeding only. Loading returns unknown.
Fixed downward camera axis; scale/translation/fovy and bounded lighting variation tested, arbitrary viewpoint not validated.
Simulator image tests do not establish real-video accuracy or physical safety.
Fine yaw/tilt boundaries are not separately calibrated; classifier does not estimate continuous yaw.
Single overhead RGB cannot prove actual release, no contact, height, or full3D stability.
Colored clutter, severe color shifts, unseen occluders, camera tilt or new brick textures may be out of distribution.
Boundary abstentions are intended; visual success alone never completes the physical task.
